reason: The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates M–N bond formation and enhanced durability in an N–Pt/HEA electrocatalyst under electrochemical conditions, but it does not address automotive exhaust environments, exposure to H2O and NO, thermal aging, or low-PGM consumption in that context. The key premises about stabilization against thermal/chemical degradation and performance in exhaust are extrapolations without direct support.
premises: Nitrogen treatment of a multi-element alloy can form stable metal–nitrogen bonds on the surface.
Metal–nitrogen bonds stabilize the high-entropy structure against thermal and chemical degradation.
Stabilization by M–N bonds reduces surface metal leaching and sintering.
M–N bonds mitigate adverse phase changes during exposure to H2O, NO, and thermal cycling.
These effects translate to maintained catalytic activity and durability in automotive exhaust conditions.
